Book Title: What If You Had Animal Eyes!? (Scholastic Reader, Level 2)
Author: Sandra Markle, Howard McWilliam
Categories (Amazon): Books > Children's Books > Literature & Fiction > Chapter Books & Readers > Beginner Readers
Summary: If you could have any animal's eyes, whose would you choose? What if you woke up one morning and your eyes weren't yours? Sandra Markle's bestselling What If You Had... series is now in Scholastic's Level 2 reader format! Perfect for kids just learning to read independently, this imaginative book explores what would happen if you looked in the mirror and saw a pair of animal eyes instead of your own. From the chameleon's eyes that can point in different directions, to the colossal squid's eyes that shine in the dark, discover what it would be like if you had these special eyes. Then, find out why your eyes are just the right ones for you!

Book Title: What If You Had Animal Teeth?
Author: Sandra Markle, Howard McWilliam
Categories (Amazon): Books > Children's Books > Growing Up & Facts of Life > Health > Daily Activities
Summary: If you could have any animal's front teeth, whose would you choose? WHAT IF YOU HAD ANIMAL TEETH takes children on a fun, informative, and imaginative journey as they explore what it would be like if their own front teeth were replaced by those of a different animal. Featuring a dozen animals (beaver, great white shark, narwhal, elephant, rattlesnake, naked mole rat, hippopotamus, crocodile, and more), this book explores how different teeth are especially adapted for an animal's survival. At the end of the book, children will discover why their own teeth are just right for them. And they'll also get a friendly reminder to take good care of their teeth, because they're the only teeth they'll ever have. Each spread features a photograph of the animal using its specialized teeth on the left and a humorous illustrated image of a child using that animal's teeth on the right.
Customer Reviews (Text): Customers find this book engaging and filled with cool facts about animal teeth, with 32 pages packed with information. The illustrations are well-received, with one customer noting how the animal features and imaging through illustrations capture children's interest. Customers appreciate the book's humor and creativity, with one mentioning how it helps children think about animal adaptations.
Editorial Reviews (Text): From Booklist Losing a first tooth is a memorable milestone in the life of a young person. Markle uses this universal experience to pose a relevant, though slightly unsettling, scientific inquiry: “But what if an animal’s teeth grew in, instead?” In a fashion germane to her audience, she presents interesting animal trivia via examples and common happenings in their own lives—for example, if you had naked mole rat teeth, you could operate them separately like chopsticks. McWilliam’s huge-jawed illustrations, such as a young Inuit fishing with a narwhal tusk or a frustrated student mowing through his math book with a beaver’s orange-colored incisors, are somehow both hilarious and terrifying. Meanwhile, photos of open-mouthed animals accompany the text. Though perhaps not the best choice for the nightmare-prone, this will surely satisfy animal enthusiasts and trivia lovers, and dentists and parents will appreciate the mention of ways to keep human chompers healthy.
